especially across the Tuesday-Thursday time period. Hurricane Polo 
in the Pacific is soon expected to be steered northeast and into the 
Southern Plains by an approaching southwest U.S. trough. The outer 
plume of moisture by this hurricane is likely to stretch north and 
into the local area by Wednesday. This increase in moisture content 
across the area will enhance precipitation efficiency across the 
middle to end of the week (PWAT values as high as 1.75-2"...over 2 
times greater than the average end of september values around 
0.75").  

The earliest arrival for precipitation this week now looks to come 
Tuesday. Between Tuesday and Thursday, multiple rounds of widespread 
rain showers will be expected to lift north and up across all of 
central Kansas/Nebraska. Though steady precipitation chances 
generally hold across all three days, the highest confidence window 
and peak rainfall amounts will look to come across the Wednesday and 
Wednesday night period when the surface low is closest to the area 
(crossing through southern Kansas). This low will continue to push 
east and away across the day Thursday, leaving the most uncertainty 
within the first arrival window of showers on Tuesday and the last 
lingering bands of precipitation on Thursday. 

The latest NBM QPF guidance project between 2-4" of precipitation to 
fall across the area over this three day period with the locally 
heavier amounts generally concentrated towards the south and east 
(locations closer to the system center). It is important to know that 
some guidance has suggested a slightly further northward track of this 
system that could shift our forecast amounts northward. If this 
northward trend continues, areas north of I-80 could overachieve 
current expectations with the far south and southeast portions of 
the area underachieving expectations.  

For far northern portions of the area (locations north of I-80), 
through the mean/most likely value is around 2-2.5" of 
precipitation, a large gap separates the high end (75th percentile) 
and the low end (25th percentile) model guidance (spread of the NBM 
ensemble). In fact the low end values (25% percentile where 75% of 
the guidance exceeds) is around 1.25-1.75" with the upper limit 
(75th percentile where only 25% of the guidance exceeds) is between 
2-4". This high range comes from the fact where central Nebraska is 
likely to find itself within the outer bounds of the system. 
Precipitation amounts for these locations are the most susceptible 
to the system track (sharp precipitation gradient). A north or south 
shift of the system track can vastly effect precipitation amounts 
across the "fringes" compared to locations across central Kansas 
that lie closer to the system center track. In comparison, the 
portions of the forecast area with the higher end forecast 
precipitation amounts (3-4" for north central Kansas and Nebraska 
areas southeast of the Tri-Cities), have the lower end guidance 
(25th percentile) around 2-2.75" with the upper end guidance (75th 
percentile) around 3.5-4". Within the last 24-hours, the confidence 
in the higher-end amounts have seemed to diminish some. If this 
trend continues, it is possible for forecast amounts to also 
decrease in the upper bounds. 

Given the anomalously high moisture concentration with the large 
window of steady rain showers, the WPC has included the entire area 
underneath a Slight Risk of Excessive Rainfall (15-40% chance of 
rainfall exceeding flash flood guidance within 25 miles of a point) 
for Tuesday and Wednesday.  

Besides the precipitation potential this week, temperatures look to 
be on track to steadily decrease a few degrees. Given the 
continuation of mostly cloudy skies across much of the week 
(primarily through Thursday) and the passage of a cold front Tuesday 
night, temperatures are forecast to peak between the upper 50s and 
70s each day this week. Highs could reach their coolest point for 
the week around Friday (upper 50s to mid 60s). Overnight lows in the 
mid 40s to low 50s appear possible to achieve both Thursday and 
Friday nights.
